title: Waste
subtitle: 「垃圾／廢料／殘骸／殘留物／副產品」，究竟是哪一種 waste？
description: 「垃圾／廢料／殘骸／殘留物／副產品」，究竟是哪一種 waste？

words.note: 使用者提供。rubbish 是英式英語中非常常見的日常用語，指不再需要、要丟棄的東西，尤其是家庭或一般生活垃圾。美式英語更常用 trash 或 garbage。
words.example: Please put the rubbish in the bin.

options.explanation: household collection + British council context naturally favours rubbish.

falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Put the rubbish in the bin. The factory generates industrial waste.

falseSynonyms.zh: refuse 是較正式的垃圾／廢物名詞，常見於 municipal collection/disposal；日常口語較少。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The council manages refuse collection. There is rubbish beside the bin.

falseSynonyms.zh: scrap 通常是製造、金屬或拆卸留下且可能仍可回收的材料；不是所有 waste 都是 scrap。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The company sells scrap metal. Food waste goes to composting.

falseSynonyms.zh: debris 是破壞、事故、風暴或拆卸後的碎片；普通家居垃圾不叫 debris。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Debris covered the road after the storm. Household rubbish is collected weekly.

falseSynonyms.zh: residue 是程序後留下的殘留物；它未必被棄置，也不等於所有 waste。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON A sticky residue remained on the surface. The site produces construction waste.

falseSynonyms.zh: by-product 是附帶產物，可能有價值並被再利用；稱為 waste 會更強地暗示無用或待處置。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Heat is a by-product of the process. The process also creates waste for disposal.

falseSynonyms.zh: litter 專指被隨意丟在公共地方的垃圾；正常收集、裝袋或工業 waste 不一定是 litter。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Please do not drop litter. The factory produces waste material.

falseSynonyms.zh: wastage 通常指浪費掉的數量、損耗或不必要消耗，不等於一堆實體垃圾。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Better cutting reduced material wastage. The offcuts were collected as waste.
